Subject: Re: Discovery — Redwood fit for Acme Analytics

Hi Sarah — thanks again for a constructive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Economic buyer: you indicated CFO Tom Rivera will sign off on pricing and org-level SLAs.
- Security/legal contacts: CISO Daniel Park + Procurement (Ilya Mendes) will run vendor security and commercial review; you said initial SOC 2 + data handling questionnaire is required.
- Decision criteria: (1) predictable per-token cost & autoscaling, (2) private deployment option for PII workloads, (3) SLA on latency for live feature.

Proposed routing and sequencing (what we typically do; flexible):
1) NDA (two-way) — get signed so we can share full S3 logs and security artifacts.
2) Security materials & DPA template — we provide SOC2, DPA draft, and we’re happy to walk your security team through the controls.
3) Commercial term sheet / MSA — start parallel redline but keep MSA subservient to DPA items that may affect scope.

Next concrete items from our side: 
- I attached a short call notes PDF (discovery-notes-20260601.pdf).
- I’ll send our standard two-way NDA via DocuSign today (expected turn: 1–2 business days).
- Marcus will outline recommended redline sequencing for MSA/DPA to minimize back-and-forth.

Can you confirm the best person at Acme to receive the NDA (procurement vs legal) and whether Tom wants pricing options in a separate commercial deck or inside the MSA?

Thanks,
Jasmine

Jasmine — thanks for the summary and the notes. Short answers from our side: 

- NDA recipient: please send NDA to procurement (procurement@acmeanalytics.com) and cc Daniel (CISO) and me. Procurement will triage then send to legal if needed.
- Review cadence: procurement/legal usually take ~7–10 business days for standard NDAs; DPAs/MSAs take longer depending on redlines.
- Economic buyer: Tom will want a short pricing options sheet to review before MSA; he expects a 2–3 option view (baseline, optimized quantization, private-hosted).

Regarding security review: Daniel would like the SOC 2 Type II report and a short summary mapping of where data is stored and who has access. If you can include a brief DPA draft we can start internal redlines in parallel to the NDA.

Thanks — I’ll stand by for the DocuSign NDA.

Jasmine / Laura — quick internal note on routing and suggested sequencing to minimize legal friction: 

1) Send two-way NDA via DocuSign to procurement@acmeanalytics.com (cc Daniel Park). This unlocks access to SOC2 and network diagrams. Keep NDA narrowly scoped to evaluation data only. Typical turn: 3 business days if procurement is responsive.
2) Parallel: send DPA draft + short data map (where tokens log, retention defaults, encryption at rest/in-transit) to Daniel. Ask for security touchpoint meeting (30 min) the same week NDA is signed.
3) MSA commercial redlines can be initiated and shared with Tom and Procurement but explicitly call out any sections that depend on the DPA (data residency, deletion, subprocessor list).

I attached our recommended redline sequence matrix (redline-sequence.xlsx) and a copy of the NDA template we typically use (NDA-Acme-Template.docx). Note: if Acme wants to use their house NDA, push for a short review and try to keep it to 5–7 business days for signature.

If we follow this flow, we should be able to get to a commercial term sheet within ~3 weeks and an MSA signature in 4–6 weeks, assuming normal procurement/LEGAL SLAs. I’ll draft the DocuSign envelope and share the link once Jasmine confirms recipients.

—Marcus

Sarah — following internal alignment here’s the agreed plan and asks so we have clear ownership and SLAs: 

1) NDA (DocuSign) — I’ve prepared a two-way NDA and will send to procurement@acmeanalytics.com (cc Daniel Park and you) now. Requested signers: Acme procurement + Redwood legal. Target turn: 3 business days. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/nda/ABC123

2) Security package & DPA draft — Marcus will attach the DPA draft and a 1-page data map once NDA is complete. Ask: Daniel, can you confirm preferred DPA contact and whether your legal prefers a starter template from Acme or ours?

3) Commercial options for Tom — I’ll upload a 2–3 option pricing sheet to HubSpot (link below) and send a short explainer deck. Ask: Sarah, would Tom prefer a single-page executive summary or a short deck for his review?

4) Timeline expectation: procurement/legal 5–10 business days per doc (NDA faster), DPA/MSA 10–20 business days depending on redlines. We’ll keep commercial negotiations running in parallel to avoid blocking.

Related links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/ACME-2026-049), DocuSign NDA (https://docusign.com/nda/ABC123), discovery notes drive (https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/ACME-discovery-notes)

Thanks — we’ll await procurement confirmation and kick off the security touchpoint as soon as the NDA is signed.
